rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 46:20 narrows the preceding summary of both groups’ fates to the arrogant Quraysh.
rows.anchor: specifically addresses the arrogant among the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant will be brought before Hell and told that worldly favors are spent; humiliating torment follows their baseless arrogance and disobedience.
rows.anchor: fully benefited in the previous world from the favours ordained for them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude to God and fulfilling creatures’ rights turn worldly blessings into further favors for the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: show gratitude to God and fulfill the rights of His creatures, they gather more favours for the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant use up their share of blessings in this life and are punished later for neglecting their obligations toward them.
rows.anchor: they consume their quota of favours in this very world; in the Hereafter, they will be punished for not fulfilling their obligations towards these favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God grants all blessings, people have no right to act arrogantly after receiving them.
rows.anchor: since God blesses them with all the favours, what right has a person to show such behaviour after receiving them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride would be fitting only for someone who originated something and acquired it through personal ability without God’s role.
rows.anchor: he himself is the originator of something and without any role played by God acquires something on the basis of his own personal ability

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given that everything is God-given, pride is foolish, and using God’s gifts to disobey Him is even more foolish.
rows.anchor: When everything is God-given, then showing pride is absolute foolishness and ignorance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section depicts the denial and fate of ‘Ād to assure the Prophet and warn arrogant Quraysh that persistence will bring the same fate.
rows.anchor: to assure the Prophet (sws) and to warn the arrogant Quraysh that if they do not desist from their attitude, they too will end up with a similar fate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “brother of ‘Ād” is the prophet Hūd, sent as a Messenger to the nation to which he belonged.
rows.anchor: hence is called the brother of the ‘ Ād

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger’s belonging to his own nation has significant bearing on the conclusive communication of truth.
rows.anchor: belongs to his own nation has many significant aspects

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lexicons define Aḥqāf as rectangular dunes; here it denotes the desert between Oman, Yemen, Najd, and Hadramawt.
rows.anchor: the desert which stretches between Oman, Yemen, Najd and Hadrmawt

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥqāf was the original homeland of the people of ‘Ād.
rows.anchor: It is the original dwelling place of the people of ‘Ād

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Aḥqāf directs attention to the great destruction that occurred there.
rows.anchor: directed attention to the great destruction that took place in this area

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At ‘Ād’s height, the region was likely lush and marked by major cultural achievements; it is now a desolate desert.
rows.anchor: this area would have been very green and lush and impregnated with those great cultural feats

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author proposes that Aḥqāf was named after ‘Ād’s decline, when dunes replaced its monumental structures.
rows.anchor: in place of majestic structures only sand dunes remained

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about warners before and behind Hūd is parenthetical, and nadheer is the plural of nadheer, “warner.”
rows.anchor: are a parenthetical sentence. The word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd’s warning was not new: warners and signs of threatened punishment had already come to territories before and after his.
rows.anchor: the warnings sounded by the Prophet Hūd (sws) are nothing new. Warners have already come to territories in front of his and those behind it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier and later generations alike failed to heed their respective warners.
rows.anchor: just as the earlier generations did not take heed from their respective warners, these later generations also did not benefit from the warnings of their warner

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd’s central warning was to worship God alone and fear the torment of a dreadful day if they persisted in worshipping others.
rows.anchor: asked them not to worship anyone other than God; if they do not desist from worshipping others besides God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheism is the root of evil from which all other evils branch.
rows.anchor: the real basis of evil is polytheism. From this evil springs the branches of all other evils

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s messengers foreground the warning against polytheism and tell people that persistence brings divine punishment.
rows.anchor: the Messengers of God have informed their people about it the foremost and have told them that if people do not desist from it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheism is high treason against God, and a people given conclusive truth receives no further respite if it persists in it.
rows.anchor: Polytheism on this earth is no less than high treason against God. For this reason, the nation to which God conclusively delivers the truth is not granted further respite

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afk means “to tell a lie”; with ʿan it also carries the sense of turning someone away from something.
rows.anchor: shows that this word encompasses the meaning of another word

rows.speaker: people of ‘Ād
rows.claim: They accuse Hūd of trying to turn them from their gods by lying.
rows.anchor: they answer the Prophet Hūd (sws) by exclaiming that he has come to them as a messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author completes the people’s accusation: they call Hūd’s messengerhood and punishment threat a bluff to turn them from their deities, demanding the doom as proof.
rows.anchor: to bluff them about his messengerhood as well as about a punishment in order to turn them away from their deities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows the punishment’s timing and form; Hūd has delivered his message, while their demand for the doom displays ignorance.
rows.anchor: only God has their knowledge; he does not have any information about them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “they saw it” refers back to the punishment mentioned in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: the punishment mentioned in the previous verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀriḍ means “cloud” and functions grammatically as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl).
rows.anchor: and here it is an accusative of state (ḥāl)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the cloud headed toward their valleys, the people rejoiced, mistaking it for a rain cloud.
rows.anchor: they were overjoyed remarking that it was a rain-drenched cloud that will drench their valleys

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud was instead the punishment they had sought to hasten.
rows.anchor: what they thought to be a rain-drenched cloud was, on the contrary, the punishment they wanted to hasten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment was a stormy wind containing torment; Sūrah al-Ḥāqqah describes ‘Ād destroyed by an uncontrollable storm over seven nights and eight days.
rows.anchor: they were destroyed by an uncontrollable storm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tempest left no visible trace of ‘Ād except their destroyed dwellings.
rows.anchor: nothing except the signs of their destroyed dwellings could be seen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s punishment of wrongdoers is an enduring law, so Quraysh will meet ‘Ād’s fate if they adopt the same attitude.
rows.anchor: the fact is that the Almighty always punishes the wrongdoers in such a fashion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Ād had far greater resources, power, and building ability than Quraysh, yet could not save themselves when God seized them.
rows.anchor: much more than what the Quraysh possessed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ‘Ād had hearing, sight, and intellect, these faculties did not help because they rejected God’s signs; the torment they mocked engulfed them.
rows.anchor: since they were not prepared to accept the light of God’s revelations, their ears, eyes and hearts could be of no avail to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true light of hearing, sight, and hearts comes from God’s revelations.
rows.anchor: the real light of the ears, eyes and hearts is produced by the revelations of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without revelation’s radiance, people perceive only the apparent and tangible, and devote their effort to material gain.
rows.anchor: If these faculties are not lit up by the radiance of God’s revelations, they can only feel and see the apparent and the tangible

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enslavement to material appearances dulls the faculties, preventing reflection beyond the tangible and recognition that deeper deliberation is needed.
rows.anchor: people spend all their might to earn material benefits. The result of being slaves to the apparent and the tangible is that these abilities and faculties become rusty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aspect of things that calls for real deliberation lies beyond what is apparent and tangible.
rows.anchor: the real aspect that requires deliberation is the one beyond what is the apparent and the tangible
